# Copilot instructions

## Build and validation

This is a Jekyll site based on the al-folio theme. Ruby/Bundler builds the site; npm only provides Prettier and its Liquid plugin.

- Install dependencies: `bundle install` and `npm ci`. Native builds also require ImageMagick and Jupyter; CI installs Jupyter with `pip3 install --upgrade jupyter`.
- Recommended local server: `docker compose up` (or `docker compose up --build` after changing Ruby/system dependencies), then open `http://localhost:8080`. The container watches files and restarts Jekyll when `_config.yml` changes.
- Native local server: `bundle exec jekyll serve --lsi`, then open `http://localhost:4000`. Restart it after changing `_config.yml`.
- Production build: set `JEKYLL_ENV=production`, run `bundle exec jekyll build --lsi`, then optionally run `npx purgecss -c purgecss.config.js`. Output is generated in `_site/`.
- CI-equivalent build dependencies include global `mermaid.cli` and `purgecss`; deployment is handled by `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and GitHub Pages. Do not use the destructive legacy `bin/deploy` script for routine deployment.
- Format check: `npx prettier . --check`; format files with `npx prettier . --write`.
- Check one file: `npx prettier _pages/about.md --check` (replace the path with the file being changed).
- Optional pre-commit checks: `pre-commit run --all-files`; run one hook with `pre-commit run check-yaml --all-files`.
- There is no unit-test framework. The production Jekyll build is the primary integration check. CI additionally checks Markdown/HTML links with Lychee and supports a manual Axe accessibility workflow. For a targeted accessibility check, serve `_site/` and run `axe http://localhost:8080/<path>/ --load-delay=1500 --exit`.

## Architecture

- `_config.yml` is the central integration point: site identity, navigation/features, collections, Jekyll plugins, Scholar behavior, responsive-image generation, CDN versions, and external data loading all flow from it.
- Content lives primarily in `_pages/`, `_news/`, `_projects/`, `_bibliography/papers.bib`, and `_data/`. Front matter selects a layout and controls navigation or layout-specific behavior.
- Rendering is layered: pages/collection documents select `_layouts/*.liquid`; layouts compose reusable `_includes/*.liquid`; `_layouts/default.liquid` provides the HTML shell and loads the shared script includes.
- Styles originate at `assets/css/main.scss`, which has Jekyll front matter and imports the partials in `_sass/`. Browser behavior is in `assets/js/`, while library versions and integrity hashes are configured in `_config.yml`.
- Publications are generated by Jekyll Scholar from `_bibliography/papers.bib` through `_layouts/bib.liquid`. Author highlighting uses `scholar.first_name`/`last_name`; coauthor links come from `_data/coauthors.yml`; venue badges come from `_data/venues.yml`; `selected = {true}` controls the selected-publications block.
- Images normally go through `_includes/figure.liquid`. With ImageMagick enabled, it expects generated `-480.webp`, `-800.webp`, and `-1400.webp` variants beside supported source images. Publication previews belong in `assets/img/publication_preview/`; local publication PDFs belong in `assets/pdf/`.
- `_plugins/` contains custom Liquid tags/filters used by templates. Changes there affect the build pipeline and require a Jekyll restart.

## Repository conventions

- Use `.liquid` for layouts/includes and preserve Liquid whitespace-control syntax where present. Prettier is configured with `@shopify/prettier-plugin-liquid`, a 150-column width, and ES5 trailing commas.
- Use `relative_url`/`absolute_url` filters for internal paths so links continue to work if `baseurl` changes. Use the existing cache-busting filters for local CSS, JS, and image assets loaded by templates.
- New pages go in `_pages/` with explicit `layout`, `title`, and `permalink`; set `nav`, `nav_order`, and page-specific flags only when the page should participate in those features.
- News files use front matter with `layout: post`, a date, and `inline: true` for text rendered directly in the news list. Linked/non-inline news is supported by the theme but should follow existing front-matter patterns.
- Publication metadata should be edited in `papers.bib`, not duplicated in page Markdown. Preview names are bare filenames resolved under `assets/img/publication_preview/`; fields such as `doi`, `eprint`, `pdf`, `code`, and `selected` directly control links and rendering.
- Coauthor keys in `_data/coauthors.yml` are lowercase, accent-stripped last names because `_layouts/bib.liquid` normalizes names before lookup. Each entry lists accepted first-name forms.
- Treat `_site/`, `.jekyll-cache/`, and responsive WebP files produced by a build as generated output. Do not hand-edit `_site/`; change source content/templates/configuration and rebuild.
- Preserve this repository's personal content and configuration rather than reintroducing generic al-folio sample data. Upstream README/INSTALL text describes the theme broadly and can be stale relative to this repository's Docker and GitHub Pages configuration.
